title: Municipality Reports
text:
Search for a municipality below and open its report. Municipality reports summarize all commercial and industrial PINs located in that municipality, including municipalities that cross township boundaries.

title: PINs to Projects
text:
This website documents how individual Property Index Numbers (PINs) were grouped into larger commercial and industrial property projects.


Browse by Township
Search for a township and open the township report containing its commercial and industrial PINs.
Browse townships


Browse by municipality
Search for a municipality and open the township report or reports containing its commercial and industrial PINs.
Browse municipalities


Find a PIN or Project
Search for a PIN, municipality, township, project key PIN, or appellant.
Search PINs


How the data are organized
Read how PINs, key PINs, projects, municipalities, and townships relate to one another.
Read the documentation

title: How PINs Relate to Projects
text:
A PIN identifies an individual tax parcel. A single commercial or industrial development may contain several parcels and therefore several PINs.
A project is the broader property grouping created from the available appeal records, sale documents, valuation worksheets, and parcel proximity. The manually assigned key PIN identifies that grouped project.

title: How PINs Relate to Projects
text:
A PIN identifies an individual tax parcel. A single commercial or industrial development may contain several parcels and therefore several PINs.
A project is the broader property grouping created from the available appeal records, sale documents, valuation worksheets, and parcel proximity. The manually assigned key PIN identifies that grouped project.

title: How PINs Relate to Projects
text:
Geographic organization
Each PIN is associated with a municipality and a township. The detailed reports are rendered by township because the parcel analysis was written around township boundaries and because there are substantially fewer townships than municipalities.
Municipal boundaries and township boundaries do not always match. A municipality may therefore appear in more than one township report. The municipality directory lists every relevant township report rather than pretending each municipality belongs to exactly one township.

title: How PINs Relate to Projects
text:
Using the site
Use Municipalities when you know the municipality name. Use Search PINs when you know a PIN, project key PIN, appellant, township, or municipality. Both pages link to the pre-rendered township reports.

title: Township Reports
text:
Search for a township below and open its report. Township reports summarize the commercial and industrial PINs and projects located within each township.
Because projects may cross municipal or township boundaries, report counts are not additive across geographies.
